title: 2026 Q3 QBR - Cygnus Retail Health Check
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: zoom.us/rec/share/abc123 (private)
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Cygnus), Sara Nguyen (Cygnus), Marcus Lee (Cygnus), Renee Alvarez (Cygnus), Jamal Brooks (Cygnus)
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage trends, cost optimization, reliability incidents, upcoming roadmap alignment and renewal path. Cygnus has grown usage 28% q/q driven by personalized recommendations; costs are steady but a couple of high-latency tails noted. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for peak traffic, VPC requirements for compliance, and plan for a pilot on 4-node Dedicated pool. Action items: share detailed cost breakdown, schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff, provide SOC2 / architecture docs, run latency p99 benchmark with sample dataset.
topics: Usage trends and embeddings/LLM call mix
Cost drivers and optimization opportunities (batching, quantization)
Reliability incidents and mitigation (p99 latency spikes, autoscaling tuning)
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick qbr and health check, thanks for carving out the time
[00:18] Liam (Cygnus): no problem, excited to see the numbers, we've been ramping up recommendations this quarter
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood CSM): quick note, i'll recap action items at the end and drop the deck, and we'll link the SOC2 and architecture notes
[00:48] Maya (Redwood SE): we pulled usage from your account, Cygnus – 28% q over q increase, embeddings are now 42% of calls mainly for product similarity and reranking
[01:12] Sara (Cygnus): yea embeddings spiked after the new mobile rollout, cost hit us a bit in july, jamal had a question on that later
[01:30] Jamal (Cygnus Finance): yeah we saw a couple of big line items, curious what the biggest levers are to reduce unit costs without hurting latency
[01:47] Maya: short answer: prefix caching, batching, and quantization profiles. We saw good wins on similar workloads by enabling automatic prefix/K-V cache and moving certain models to int8 quantized variants
[02:10] Marcus (Cygnus): small nit – when you say K-V cache, we saw the transcript call it KV cache but our infra team calls it k-v, no big deal
[02:25] Ethan: totally, sorry transcription aside. For Cygnus specifically, there's a long tail on p99 for sessions that go beyond 1k tokens which is driving cost on the larger models
[02:45] Sara: is that from chat style flows or batch inference?
[02:50] Maya: mostly interactive sessions – multi-turn dialog for product discovery. For batch recommendation reranks we have better batching. The interactive flows are where latency matters, p50 is still great but p99 spikes
[03:12] Liam: can you quantify p99? our SLO is 200ms for interactive calls, we saw some 800–1,200ms outliers last month
[03:28] Maya: current p99 for your primary gen model is ~820ms on Hosted during peak – that aligns with what you saw. We traced a few spikes to autoscale warmup and to large context windows causing kernel fallbacks
[03:45] Marcus: any quick mitigation we can apply? we need to keep under the SLO during Black Friday prep
[03:55] Ethan: immediate: we can enable request shaping on your routes to prioritize latency-sensitive traffic, and second, move high-volume routes to a reserved Dedicated pool for predictable throughput
[04:18] Sara: Dedicated = reserved GPUs, right? what's the lift for us to try that?
[04:25] Maya: yes Dedicated is GPU-reserved capacity. For lift, we run a short pilot: provisioning + a canary routing rule. For Cygnus we'd recommend a 4-node pool to start, we can size based on your peak qps traces
[04:44] Liam: timeline?
[04:46] Maya: we can provision in one week in our hosted region, then a 2-week canary, so 3 weeks from greenlight to having real traffic on Dedicated
[05:00] Renee (Product): how do fallbacks work if Dedicated gets saturated? we can't have errors in production
[05:08] Ethan: good point — we have automatic fallback policies: during saturation we route to a compatible model variant in Hosted that meets latency/cost constraints; policy is configurable per route
[05:22] Jamal: finance wants TCO comparison — do you have a sample calc?
[05:28] Jordan: yes i'll share a TCO spreadsheet; we can run a side-by-side: hosted variable cost vs reserved commit (Dedicated) amortized plus overages. We'll include assumptions for batching gains and expected latency improvements
[05:46] Marcus: on compliance – we need VPC + KMS + audit logs for payment data. Are you able to support private deployment?
[05:56] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and customer KMS/HSM integrations; SOC2 audit logs and enhanced retention are part of the enterprise package
[06:10] Sara: do you have a template architecture for Private? we'd want to show our security team
[06:16] Jordan: absolutely — i'll send the Private deployment arch diagram and SOC2 artifact links after the call (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/priv-deploy). We'll also include our compliance checklist
[06:31] Liam: perfect. About reliability incidents – we had two mid-july incidents where embeddings throughput dropped ~30% for ~45 minutes, any root cause identified?
[06:44] Maya: we investigated – it looked like a node OOM on a GPU pool after a bad autoscaler configuration; we pushed a fix to the autoscaler policy and added better node-level metrics and alerting
[06:58] Ethan: i added those incident notes to the ticket we shared, and we recommend setting higher alert thresholds for GPU memory pressure and configuring graceful draining for scale-in
[07:12] Marcus: will that require code changes on our side?
[07:16] Maya: no changes required; it's infra/config updates. We'll also onboard you to the new tracing hooks so your SEs can see KV miss rates and kernel fallbacks
[07:30] Sara: that tracing would be helpful. can the traces be routed to our datadog?
[07:35] Maya: yep we support sending traces and metrics to datadog and prometheus endpoints, we'll include the setup steps
[07:44] Liam: switching to roadmap – are there any upcoming features that will help our recommendations use case?
[07:50] Maya: upcoming Q4 features: improved continuous batching for embeddings, cheaper int4 experimental profiles for smaller models, and a per-route latency SLO enforcement which will help enforce the 200ms SLO
[08:06] Renee: int4 — is that ready for production?
[08:09] Maya: int4 is experimental; we've had early customers in private pilot. We'll include recommended guardrails and fallback profiles if you want to test it in a canary
[08:22] Jamal: curious about model versions — we saw a small degrade after the 2026-06 model update, how do you manage rollouts?
[08:31] Ethan: we support canary and phased rollouts with automatic fallback if quality metrics drop; we tie rollouts to evals and prompt sets, and you can pin model versions per route
[08:44] Sara: can you run an eval on our prompt set for the next update? we have a 1,000 prompt regression deck
[08:50] Maya: yes we can run a QA eval; we'll need the prompt deck and expected outputs. Jordan, can we own delivery?
[08:57] Jordan: yes we'll run the eval and share the results within 10 business days
[09:06] Liam: re: costs — any quick low-hanging wins?
[09:11] Maya: switch bigger batch jobs to off-peak windows, enable caching for repeated prompts, move non-latency critical models to quantized variants. For embeddings, enable caching of similarity vectors at the app layer so you reduce re-embeds
[09:28] Marcus: we've already cached at the app layer for 60% of lookups, we'll increase that. Any thoughts on autoscaling thresholds?
[09:36] Maya: raise scale-up threshold slightly and add a small buffer of reserved capacity for typical peak — that avoids cold starts. We can share tuned configs from similar retail customers
[09:47] Sara: about the Dedicated pilot — what metrics do we capture to decide if we convert to a commit?
[09:54] Ethan: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1M tokens, error rates, and availability. Also measure improvement in tail latency and cart conversion lift (if you want business metrics)
[10:09] Liam: sounds good. Who owns the pilot execution?
[10:12] Maya: Redwood SE will own provisioning and routing config; Cygnus infra will validate VPC rules and run traffic; CSM (Jordan) will own success criteria and reporting
[10:23] Renee: any special considerations for our GDPR data residency needs?
[10:27] Maya: we can pin workloads to eu-west regions and enable data residency controls; for Private we can also offer on-prem packaging if required
[10:36] Jamal: renewal timing — our contract renews in november, are we thinking about expansion or same seat + Dedicated?
[10:44] Ethan: early discussion but given growth, a Dedicated conversion is likely. We'll propose a phased commit that starts with a pilot and then converts to a 12-month reserved agreement if metrics meet targets
[10:58] Liam: any competitors we should be worried about?
[11:02] Sara: we evaluated Anthropic and our internal infra; Anthropic priced out higher but had lower latency in some cases
[11:11] Ethan: noted — we'll include a competitive note. We also compare to building in-house which has higher ops burden
[11:20] Marcus: quick question — can you share the p99 latency histograms for last 30 days?
[11:25] Jordan: yes i'll attach them to the follow-up email and add a shared folder with dashboards
[11:32] Liam: can we run the p99 benchmark you mentioned with our 1k token flows?
[11:36] Maya: we recommend a 4-hour benchmark with synthetic and replay traffic; we'll coordinate windows with your infra to avoid business hours impact
[11:47] Renee: timeline for next steps?
[11:50] Ethan: propose to: 1) provision Dedicated pilot (week 1), 2) run canary and benchmarks (weeks 2-3), 3) review cost/TCO and decide on commit (week 4)
[12:05] Jamal: from finance side i'd like the modeled TCO before week 3, to avoid surprises
[12:12] Jordan: understood — i'll prioritize that spreadsheet and assumptions
[12:17] Sara: any risks for the Dedicated setup?
[12:21] Maya: risk is under-provisioning or mis-sized pool; we mitigate by baselining on your peak qps traces and enabling autoscale burst policies for short spikes
[12:36] Liam: okay let's talk about action items
[12:39] Jordan: action items recap coming up
[12:41] Ethan: one more quick note — we saw a couple of transcription typos in previous qbrs, so the deck will be more careful with names
[12:49] Jordan: alright recap of next steps and owners — see action items below
[13:00] [END]
next_steps: Provision Dedicated 4-node pilot (Redwood/Maya) — target week of 2026-08-17
Run p99 benchmark with 1k token flows (Redwood + Cygnus infra) — 4-hour test during off-peak
Share TCO spreadsheet and cost breakdown (Jordan) — by 2026-08-20
Send SOC2 and Private deployment architecture (Jordan) — within 2 business days
Run eval on Cygnus 1,000 prompt deck (Redwood SE) — results in 10 business days
